clinician.trajectory_summary: A 32-year-old man presented with severe right upper quadrant abdominal pain and obstructive jaundice with cholestatic liver enzyme elevation. Initial abdominal ultrasound showed cholelithiasis but normal common bile duct diameter without bile duct obstruction. MRCP demonstrated a pedunculated broad-based mass lesion in the second part of the duodenum inseparable from the ampulla of Vater, with two small calculi in the lower common bile duct. Endoscopic ultrasound biopsy revealed a submucosal lesion composed of epithelioid, spindle, and ganglion-like cells with positivity for S100, synaptophysin, and chromogranin immunostaining. These histopathological and immunohistochemical features were diagnostic of gangliocytic paraganglioma. The hospital course was complicated by suspected cholangitis treated successfully with intravenous and oral antibiotics and biliary stent placement to relieve obstruction. Staging CT confirmed an ampullary mass with enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes and no thoracic involvement. The patient improved clinically and was discharged on oral antibiotics. Definitive surgical treatment and long-term follow-up were not documented in the available evidence.
